correctness.rationale: Three-neighborliness and the 90 tetrahedra leave exactly 36 missing four-sets. Four vertices are the first possible support for a 2-cycle. An explicit integral 2-cocycle vanishes on all 90 tetrahedral boundaries and evaluates ±1 on every one of the 36 missing tetrahedral spheres, proving nontriviality and primitivity. Exhaustive permutation checks prove the automorphism and sign-action assertions; mod-two chain ranks independently verify the unique nonzero H2(F2) class.

value.rationale: The minimal nine-vertex CP2 is a canonical extremal triangulation, and H2=Z is its central integral topological feature. Classifying the smallest possible vertex supports of a generator is a natural combinatorial systolic question. The answer is maximally structured: every missing tetrahedron is primitive, and the full symmetry group acts through a nontrivial sign character. This is more than a face count or recomputation of known homology.
